findings.text: RDMA cgroup lifecycle allocates a zeroed container with an empty pool list and returns its subsystem state or a memory failure, frees by draining every pool owned by the group then releasing the container, offlines by forcing limits to maximum, and publishes all three handlers plus one shared file table for both legacy and default hierarchies through the subsystem descriptor.

RDMA cgroup control table tail exposes resource, peak, events and local events files that are hidden on the root, use sequence display handlers with distinct private selectors for current versus peak, and store persistent file positions for the two event files inside the group object before a terminator entry.

A global RDMA cgroup mutex serializes traversal of the per-group pool list during both free and offline; free uses iteration safe against removal because entries are destroyed while offline uses ordinary iteration because entries persist while limits are raised.

Per-subsystem per-CPU statistics update is a no-op when the subsystem does not use the statistics path, requires preemption disabled, and is skipped in non-maskable context on architectures without non-maskable safe compare exchange.

Enqueue first performs a racy already-queued test ordered against the concurrent flusher, then atomically claims a self-linked node by moving its successor from self to null so exactly one stacked context wins, and only the winner appends the node to the per-subsystem per-CPU backlog head.

The same per-CPU statistics node can be reentered by interrupt and non-maskable contexts and concurrently reinitialized by a flusher on another processor, so plain list insertion or processor-local compare exchange would be unsafe; losers of the global atomic claim must assume the winner will queue the node.
Public statistics refresh validates that the processor identifier is non-negative, inside the identifier range and marked possible before delegating to the internal update path.

Base processor-time accounting brackets each mutation by acquiring the per-group per-CPU record with interrupt-saving sequence protection, then closes the bracket by ending the protected region, marking the group updated on the current processor and releasing the processor reference.

Processor-time routing accumulates total execution separately from categorized fields; the nice category contributes to both nice and user totals, user contributes to user, system and interrupt categories contribute to system, force-idle contributes to its own accumulator where configured, and unknown categories leave the record unchanged.
The statistics subsystem registers its tracing helper identifier set with the tracing program type during initialization under module ownership.

Legacy compatibility mask control captures the old first mask word, removes non-blockable signals from the requested word, clones the current mask, then either adds bits, removes bits or replaces the first word depending on the operation, rejects unknown operations, installs the result and optionally returns the old word, reporting a fault for inaccessible user pointers.

Signal mask installation always strips non-blockable signals, skips the locked path when the mask is unchanged because only the owner modifies it, otherwise acquires the signal-handler spinlock with interrupts disabled to publish the new mask.

When additional signals become blocked while the caller has signal-related work and belongs to a non-empty thread group, the newly blocked subset is derived as the difference from the previous mask and offered to sibling threads before the new mask is installed and pending state is recomputed.

Pending state is considered present when job-control pending or freeze trap is set, the private queue has an unblocked signal, the shared queue has an unblocked signal, or the task is frozen; the task helper sets the pending thread flag and reports true but never clears another thread, while the current-task wrapper clears the flag only when recomputation is false and freezing is not in progress.
Signal readiness is determined by OR-ing across all mask words the pending bits that are not covered by the block mask, reporting ready when any such bit remains.

Shared-pending redistribution intersects the shared queue with the newly blocked set and returns early when empty, otherwise visits sibling threads skipping exiting ones, skips threads unable to handle the remainder, removes each visited thread handleable subset, wakes threads that gain pending work, and stops once nothing remains.

Compatibility resource-usage record carries user and system times as seconds plus microseconds followed by maximum, integral, fault, swap, block, message, signal and context-switch counters in a fixed order, produced by zeroing the narrow record, assigning each native field and copying the fixed-size result to user memory.

Compatibility bitmap transfer aligns the bit count to the narrow word boundary, derives the narrow word count, then packs or unpacks two narrow words per native word with the first narrow word as the low half and the second as the high half plus an odd tail, all inside one user-access window that reports a fault on failure.

Compatibility affinity setting allocates a kernel mask, zero-extends short user input or truncates long input to kernel size, imports the user bitmap and delegates to the scheduler setter; retrieval validates that the supplied byte length covers all processors and is narrow-word aligned, uses a zeroed mask, delegates to the scheduler getter, exports at most the requested length and returns the exported length.

Compatibility signal-set import on big-endian hosts combines pairs of adjacent narrow user words into each native word with the first as low half and the second shifted as high half, cascading downward by native word count, while other hosts copy the whole record verbatim; both report a fault for bad user memory.

Compressed kernel-configuration file is served as a world-readable proc entry whose read returns the embedded image slice with default seeking, whose registered size equals the embedded length, created at initialization and removed on cleanup.

Per-processor execution-tracking record starts with nesting one and non-maskable nesting marked non-idle where idle tracking is enabled, otherwise nesting zero, always starting in the watching state; task-idle helpers record the current processor on exit and a negative marker on entry only when both tasks-RCU and full dynamic-tick support are configured.

Kernel boundary tracking counts nesting so nested exits only decrement and nested entries only increment, while the outermost exit emits tracing and deferred quiescence handling before incrementing state to leave watching and marking task idle, and the outermost entry marks task active first, increments state to resume watching, then raises nesting and restores non-maskable nesting, with warnings for bad interrupt state, underflow and unexpected idle-task identity.

Non-maskable tracking adds one when interrupting a non-watching processor to denote the outermost handler and two when already watching; exit above one subtracts two and remains watching, exit at one clears nesting and increments state to restore non-watching with conditional task-idle marking, and entry from non-watching marks task active before incrementing state and selecting the increment.

Idle entry forwards to kernel exit with watching plus idle offsets and requires interrupts disabled, idle exit wraps kernel entry with watching minus idle offsets inside raw interrupt save and restore, interrupt entry and exit are thin non-maskable wrappers requiring disabled interrupts, interrupt-with-enabled variants add save and restore around them, and empty kernel entry and exit variants represent the configuration where tracking is compiled out.
Execution-tracking tracing uses a helper that marks literal trace names and a creation marker for trace points, gated by a statically disabled read-mostly key.
